claim_as_stated: The manuscript claims a finitely generated torsion-free discrete group G_proj with a scalar projection e in C*_r(G_proj) whose canonical trace lies strictly between 0 and 1/2. It first constructs a finite self-adjoint group-algebra matrix T over G_base with a separated nonempty upper band and a projection p0 of small unnormalized matrix trace; then G_proj=G_base*F_N and an explicit free row compress p0 to scalar e with exactly the same trace. It also claims [p0] lies outside the coefficient-free reduced assembly image. This is a report of claims, not a verification.
proof_architecture: Fix one eventual finite ell: d=2^(4ell), D=d^2, bit blocks s=10ell,r=7ell and layer sizes |A_i|=d2^H_i, |B_i|=2^H_i. Field multiplication with distinct slot coefficients recovers blocks from two evaluations. Auxiliary tower Y0 opens each current gate for expansion; universal gated tower Y# supports global word recovery.

Conditional Fourier orthogonality turns collision multiplicity bounds (10^-3 full blocks, .55 partial blocks) into a mean incidence gap. Four causal bands plus a terminal orthogonal estimate are uniform in height. Independent final matchings have exponential cut tails; a connected-cut dependency graph and asymmetric local lemma avoid the total vertex-count factor. Weighted Cheeger converts the realized cut bound to chi=1/800.

Delete rare closed gates, zero windows that could conceal smaller layers, and short cyclic paths. The surviving Y agrees in the two towers, removes o(1) of every side/layer, and long oriented words locate paths globally. Constant spaces lose at most sqrt(epsilon_ell).

Assuming cover girth at C_*H_i/log d, minimal plane diagrams and long-word recovery force short arcs and at least twenty incidences per bounded face. Euler counting proves component embeddings. Cone-chain fillings give explicit thin triangles; a fixed common root then confines every earlier overlap with a copy to one finite tree ball. Cycle spaces split as an algebraic direct sum of copy cycles, yielding a residual forest and an acyclic cone complex. Torsion-free deck stabilizers plus the periodic F_p[C_p] resolution exclude group torsion.

A high-girth support of total length O(g) has bounded Betti rank; collapsing a spanning tree reduces short holonomy to a bounded-length nontrivial pivot word. A fixed upper-unitriangular dimension detects it by a nonzero polynomial of total degree <=m-1. An integer affine nilpotent central product retains this quotient and provides graded coordinates.

A coefficient-to-Schwartz-kernel bijection supplies continuous twisted convolution idempotents. Weighted rectangular Riemann sums control both coefficient l1 defect (operator correction) and relative l2 defect (nonzero projection and identity trace). A finite magnetic representation shifts the second effective twist t to t-delta, with exact unnormalized multiplicity N. Product fibers have trace <=CN t^nf(delta-t)^nf. A moving two-layer logarithmic window makes this small against exponential geometric weights at both endpoints.

Compact templates and Fourier masks are realized by one independent voltage/weight draw per edge. Graded Følner boxes test the full regular norm in polynomial finite dimension. Ordinary empirical lists below a cutoff and a shared congruence-coset list above it keep the weight alphabet finite and o(dD). Wide independent matrix entries and Schwartz–Zippel enforce girth; centered moments kill singleton edges and bounded-cycle-rank walk encoding bounds the surviving terms. The same draws satisfy both requirements, uniformly across countably many layers.

Compression and contour bounds preserve the model upper band in the actual cover, with exactly equal equivariant fiber traces. Width-one resolvent propagation yields exponentially decreasing layer trace; it is the total projection trace, not the layer dimension, which multiplies this bound. Weighted size S tends to zero.

Trim copies to disjoint domains; Hilbert–Schmidt mass in each finite ball is <=S, and the unused forest adjacency has norm O(sqrt(|S_alphabet|/(dD)))=o(1). This transports a nonempty spectral band to finite Cayley T. For trace, use all indexed copies and their exact incidence bijection. The equivariant analysis map xi -> (E_Q xi|Q)_Q is bounded despite the nonequivariant trimming. Its kernel has a strict quadratic-form upper bound; hence global upper space injects into a small equivariant complement, giving 0<tau_N(p0)<=S<1/2.

For scalar compression, free normal forms split inputs of the row U into noncancelling disjoint outputs and cancelling inputs/outputs. Projection pointwise bounds pay each cancelling part by a=tau_N(p0), giving ||Uxi|| >=(sqrt(1-a)-sqrt(a))||xi|| on p0. Polar normalization gives scalar e=(Up0)(p0U*Up0)^-1(Up0)* with trace exactly a.

construction_ideas.mechanism: The girth tests use fixed-degree polynomial zeros while norm tests kill singleton edge occurrences in even moments. Neither event conditions on final weights being nonzero; both success requirements concern the same actual voltages and weights.
construction_ideas.possible_bridge: For a fixed candidate column set of Q(Z), attempt to certify both row-rank conditions by explicit nonzero minor polynomials and bound the determinant/column cost under the same finite integer draw. All parameter interval sizes affect integer height and quadratic occupancy, and all denominators must be paid. A probabilistic existence certificate is useful only after these costs are quantified.

claim_as_stated: For each field R,C, the manuscript claims that ZFC proves: a real-valued measurable continuum (a c-additive probability on all subsets, additive for disjoint families of size strictly less than c, vanishing on singletons) implies every infinite-dimensional Banach space has a separable infinite-dimensional quotient; CH implies failure, with counterexamples of norm density aleph_1. Consequently the unrestricted assertion is independent of ZFC relative to Con(ZFC+measurable cardinal), while the assertion restricted to density exactly aleph_1 is independent relative to Con(ZFC) alone. The negative model consistency needs only Con(ZFC). These are source claims, not independently verified theorems in this reading.
proof_architecture: Use one common analytic criterion: a quotient exists iff some closed infinite-dimensional F in X* has norm-separable evaluation image R_F(X); F may be chosen separable. Construct an exactly annihilating basic sequence with finite prefix half-normers, use its coefficient-functional span Z, and prove R_G* bounded below to obtain actual surjectivity, not merely dense range.

For the positive real implication, failure of a quotient and Dvoretzky rows force R_E(B_X) to have full continuum norm density for every separable infinite-dimensional E in X*. The c-additive full-power-set measure simultaneously sums evaluations over any smaller dense set; such summability would instead yield a quotient. Regularity then gives a separated set and Hahn–Banach functionals annihilating successive initial spans, producing a seminormalized pointwise-almost-everywhere-null family.

No l1 in E allows Odell–Rosenthal sequential bidual codes in the Polish space E^N. The pointwise limit-evaluation function is Borel, so cross evaluations vanish by ordinary Borel Fubini after pushforward. Ordered power-set measures are kept in one fixed integration order. Finite suppression inequalities hold almost surely for every rational coefficient pattern; a prefix invariant preserving all future conull sections selects one infinite unconditional basic sequence. The cited Hagler–Johnson consequence contradicts failure of a quotient.

For positive real-to-complex transfer, the real witness is transported to (X*)_R. If projection iE -> (X*)_R/E is not strictly singular, a closed complex span has bounded real coordinate projections; otherwise construct complex basic f_n and summable approximants g_n to if_n in E. A compact real correction transfers separable evaluations. The negative transfer separately uses the finite-real-direct-sum lemma then complexification.

Build a real coordinate space E on omega_1 split into countably many unbounded colors. Pure family k has s_k=k+2, r=s_k prime and q between the next conjugate and r; a mixed family handles color escape. Choose L_j,m_j with small summable theta_j=L_j^(1/r)/m_j, growing L_j/m_j, and depth margins exploiting 1/q prime <1/s.

Coherent finite ordinal closures encode rational support arrays by order positions. A countable injective code assigns each next path weight from its uncropped history. Type I uses <=L_j successive children scaled by 1/m_j; Type II combines cropped paths with l_q coefficients and disjoint active weights. Norm/projection contractivity and pure coordinate l_s upper bounds follow. A transfinite prefix argument proves E=X0* for coordinate predual X0; bounded prefixes failing to be Cauchy would be detected by arbitrarily large pure or mixed averages.

Different actual infinite paths have only finitely many common weights, so finite collections have disjoint-weight tails with l_q upper bounds modulo X0. In a block sequence, only finitely many paths can exceed a fixed threshold, giving a subsequence convergent on all actual paths. Then classify compact pointwise limits of normers: finite chains have only one potentially infinite piece, infinite chains stabilize to actual paths using a common coordinate and closure coherence. Summing distinct oscillating weights gives D <=(sum 1/m_j)D< D/8, forcing zero oscillation. Riesz–Markov plus bounded convergence extends this from the norming closure to the full block dual.

For any prescribed weight J and any block tail, obtain ||y||<=500 and phi_J(y)>=1/2. Spread blocks by a record-growth argument, then take differences of weak-Cauchy blocks to get weakly null windows. Ramsey thinning forbids four repeated hits of one path. A norming-tree recursion charges high tails, at most eight marked indices per path, and low boundary incidences sum_i d_ji<=2L_j. Singleton descent contracts by sum theta_j<1/8. Stop at depth d_J and pay finite exceptional nodes with the strict exponent margin, obtaining ||sum_(i<=L_J)x_i||<=500L_J/m_J.

Reduce an arbitrary infinite-dimensional F to a least ordinal segment where projection is bounded below; pass to one pure color if possible, otherwise all colors are strictly singular. Select successive blocks by small-restriction lemmas and a summably small perturbation, with an exact lift identity for supported paths. A breadth-first binary tree carries prescribed-weight vector/functional pairs. Different branches evaluate differently on one node while cross evaluations vanish, yielding continuum many uniformly separated restrictions on F.

Under CH label all actual paths by distinct coordinates of the next color. Path-coset l_q bounds and coordinate l_s bounds define a small B:E* -> W=E*/X0, with B*(W*) contained in the canonical image J_E(E) and closure B(X0)=V the path-coset span. For X=ker(Q-B), a geometric-series lift makes Q-B onto; its adjoint annihilator is a graph over X0 perpendicular, so X* is isomorphic to E. A norm<1 quotient argument gives closure B(X)=V. Every separable infinite-dimensional F in E has separable coordinate evaluations but nonseparable path evaluations; modding out the former and using density of BX makes all X evaluations nonseparable, excluding every separable quotient.

A measurable cardinal starts real-valued measurable; the cited Solovay measure-algebra preservation theorem and kappa random reals give real-valued measurable continuum with Choice. CH is relatively consistent via constructibility. At density aleph_1, MA_(aleph_1) implies b>aleph_1 via sigma-centered eventual-domination forcing, and the cited Saxon–Sanchez Ruiz density criterion gives the positive side in an MA+c=aleph_2 model. This lowers that restricted consistency requirement to Con(ZFC).

construction_ideas.idea: Separate sparse boundary incidence from recursively contracted bulk, with a strict exponent margin.
construction_ideas.precise_hypotheses: At each recursive node, child assignments are disjoint within one weight group, while overlaps across groups are explicitly summed. Boundary incidences satisfy sum_i d_ji<=2L_j; each path has at most eight marked columns. The contraction c0=sum theta_j<1/8 is uniform, and 1/q prime <1/s leaves a growth margin after all fixed finite-depth factors are paid.
construction_ideas.mechanism: The proof continues only singleton low-weight interactions. Small l_r charges contract level by level; marked and boundary charges are paid in l1 at <=(1+B_J)^d nodes. Parameters force the fixed finite-depth price times 1+B_J+L_J^(1/q prime) below L_J/m_J.

An explicit incidence lemma may produce a tighter quadratic-occupancy cost than counting every interaction independently.

An l_r recursion does not itself control sum_j occupancy_j^2, rank, or a common row basis.
